TLINE.TDLINE: Title
Function Role Analysis
Purpose
The Function Role Analysis report will output roles with the access to
Functions. This SCAN is useful to analyze many roles at once.
Restricting Role Scope
By Role(s): If you would like to run the analysis for specific roles,
select the radio button and fill this field with those specific role(s).
Count Roles: This button can be selected to verify the number of roles
that will be analyzed from the "Role Restriction" selection criteria
entered.
Role Business Area: If you would like to run the analysis for specific
role business areas, enter those specific role business areas here. SE
will run the analysis for all roles that belong to business areas
specified here.
Roles Changed Between: If you would like to run the analysis for
specific roles that were recently created/changed, enter the start and
end dates. SW will run the analysis for all roles that were either
created or changed between those dates.
This is useful when roles are changed and you want to check whether
there were any Function access in the recently created or changed
roles.
Show Roles (push button): You can use this button to display the roles,
based on the dates specified in "Roles Changed Between" before running
the analysis.
Analyze Single Roles: Check this checkbox to include single roles in the
analysis.
Analyze Composite Roles: Check this checkbox to include composite roles
in the analysis.
Analyze Assigned Roles Only: Check this checkbox to only include roles
that are assigned to users in the analysis.
Cross System/Remote Options
Remote System (RFC): If you would like to analyze a role(s) that exists
on a different system/client enter the appropriate RFC here. The
role(s) specified will then be analyzed on a system by system basis both
locally and on the system(s) dictated by the RFC destination(s) (for all
systems where the role(s) exists).
Only on Remote System(s): Used in conjunction with the Remote System
(RFC) option above to only analyze roles in the remote system(s)
specified by the RFC destination(s). The role(s) will not be analyzed
in the local system where the report is being executed.
Function Restriction
Function IDs: With this you can restrict the scope of the analysis to
specific Function IDs that interest you. SE will only run the analysis
for the functions that you specify here. If left blank, the scan will
run for all functions in the SOD Version.
Application Area: With this you can restrict the scope of the analysis
to specific application areas that interest you. SE will only run the
analysis for the functions that have the application areas that you
specify here. If left blank, the scan will run for all application
areas.
Function Owner: With this you can restrict the scope of the analysis to
specific owners that are a characteristic of the functions.
SOD Version: Enter the SOD matrix version to use for the analysis. This
will default to the version set in the maintenance application.
Simulation Options:
Add Roles
Simulate by Adding Roles: You can use this to simulate adding roles to
users. Using this feature, you can simulate a situation where the user
would have new roles and run Function Analysis checks with new roles,
all without actually having to make any changes to the user ID.
Source RFC: If the role(s) you want to simulate is on a different
system/client, enter the name of RFC destination where the roles exist.
SW will fetch all roles from the remote location and run the analysis.
Target RFC: If you wish to simulate adding this role to the user on a
different system/client, enter the name of RFC destination in which to
add to the user.
<ZK>,, Note: When you want the Source/Target as the local system, you
can leave the fields Blank. </>
Role From/To: Enter the role name(s) you want to simulate adding.
Remove Roles
Simulate by Removing Roles: You can use this to simulate removing roles
from users. Using this feature, you can simulate a situation where you
would remove access from the user(s) and run Function Analysis omitting
the role access, all without actually having to make any changes to the
user ID.
RFC Destination for Role: If the role(s) you want to simulate removing
is (are) on a different system/client, enter the name of RFC destination
where the roles exist. SE will fetch all roles from the remote location
and run the analysis.
Role From/To: Enter the role name(s) you want to simulate removing.
<ZU><ZH>Simulation Output:</></>
As of SE3.2 release, the Summary Output will contain columns indicating
simulation "Before" & "After" results. These columns will contain
flags indicating if the Function access existed before/after the
simulation.
In the simulate removal case where a Function would be removed and the
"After" column shows a Blank, you will not be able to drill down on the
Function ID.
If you click on the Function ID, you would get the message "This
Function doesn't exist after the change. Click the "Before" checkbox to
view". As directed, you can drill down on the "Before" column for to
see the funciton details before the role removal.
Output Format:
Radio Buttons:
<ZH>Function Summary</>: With this radio button selected, the SE report
will only display the header information of the Function; no details
will be displayed. The output has drill-down capability; so all details
can be displayed by selecting the appropriate Function ID.
<ZH>Function Details</>: With this radio button selected, the SE report
will display all details of each Function ID for every role in the
selection. Details will include: Role, RFC destination, Function,
Authorizations, Profiles, Roles, Authorization Values, etc.
The output has drill-down capability, so further details can be
displayed by selecting the appropriate cell in the ALV report.
Information like Object definition, Field definition, Possible values,
Activity Text, Transaction Text, and much more are available by
double-clicking. See documentation for the meanings of columns, cells,
sort order, etc.
Execution Options:
Dynamically Enhance Matrix: Fill this checkbox if you would like to see
the SOD conflicts that result from custom programs. Note: This will
increase processing time.
Highlight Dynamically Enhanced Conflicts: This is grayed out until the
'Dynamically Enhance Matrix' option is checked.
Show Roles without Functions: Fill this checkbox if you would like to
display a message in the output, stating there are no Functions for
roles that do not have any Function access found, but were included in
your selection criteria.
<ZK>Note: This flag will not be allowed when there are any Function
Restrictions entered in the selection or when the Function Details
Output Option is selected.</>
Background processing:
Since processing mass amounts of data would most likely cause your
session to Time-Out and create a Short Dump, SW provides you an
intuitive functionality to schedule a background job for these large
analyses.
Schedule Background Job: Hit this button to start the background job
wizard, which will guide you, step-by-step, in scheduling the background
job.
You can modify and adjust all fields in the background job wizard, but
do not change program name and variant.
Note: This button will not appear if the user lacks background job
administrative privileges (authorization object S_BTCH_ADM).
View Jobs (SM37): This button will take you to transaction SM37, in
which you can monitor your jobs. You will need access to transaction
SM37.
